issues.description: The change_summary's first sentence enumerates the v2 server list as 'Serena, mcp-openapi-schema, actionlint-mcp, HashiCorp Terraform MCP, Context7, and Exa' — naming six servers as the prior-existing set that GitNexus joins as the seventh. This is exactly accurate. However, the same change_summary block then summarizes propagations with phrases like 'The server count moves from six to seven everywhere it appears' — which is fully accurate for the document body, but the change_summary itself reads slightly oddly because it carries both the 'prior six' enumeration AND the 'moves from six to seven' phrase within the same paragraph, with no explicit linkage. A reader skimming the frontmatter may briefly wonder whether the change_summary is enumerating the new total (seven) or the prior total (six). One-line edit improves auditability of the v2→v3 delta at the frontmatter surface.
issues.evidence: Lines 14-18: 'v3 adds GitNexus MCP as the seventh named server alongside Serena, mcp-openapi-schema, actionlint-mcp, HashiCorp Terraform MCP, Context7, and Exa. The server count moves from six to seven everywhere it appears (Overview, Background, FR-1, ACs, Success Criteria targets, NFR-4 context-budget commentary, Risks, Stakeholders, Appendix).' The 'alongside' phrase enumerates exactly six prior names, and 'seventh' makes the new total clear, but the next sentence frames it as 'from six to seven' which is a separate framing. Both are correct in isolation.
issues.suggestion: Optional polish (one-line edit): tighten the second sentence to 'The total moves from six to seven (GitNexus is the new entry); every "six" / "6" / "6/6" reference is updated to "seven" / "7" / "7/7" throughout (Overview, Background, ...)' — making the count-vs-list distinction explicit. Non-blocking; the document body itself is internally consistent.

recommendations: Forward the 16 Undetermined Items (UI-1 through UI-16) verbatim to the Discovery Planning rationale brief. The two new v3 UIs (UI-15 GitNexus wiring specifics; UI-16 GitNexus install mechanism) both have clear owners and a single needed-by stage (Design Composition), and UI-16 has a Discovery-stage prerequisite (per-server install-path check) that mirrors the existing UI-2 Terraform MCP install-path discovery.

Carry forward to Blueprint composition the 2 still-open v2 findings (I-DR-010 FR-9→FR-11 prerequisite note at FR-11 body; I-DR-011 AC-FR-11-d artifact-content-vs-runtime framing). I-DR-011 in particular may be resolved by replacement when the Blueprint expresses AC-FR-11-d as a Blueprint-author / KB-author instruction rather than a runtime AC (matching the v2 absorption pattern of v1's I-DR-006 at UI-7).

The new v3 Risks table entries (lines 542-543) for 'GitNexus install path is non-trivial' and 'GitNexus fallback exercised silently rather than operator-visibly' are well-shaped and mirror existing entry styles. The fallback-visibility risk is a particularly important addition because it commits the Blueprint to a specific operator-visibility design choice (per AC-FR-9-d) for the ADR-0018 fallback exercise.

The PRD v3 demonstrates exemplary single-vector scope-extension discipline: every textual touchpoint of the six→seven count is propagated, every section that names servers carries the GitNexus addition with an inline cross-reference to UI-15 or UI-16 where applicable, and the narrowing of UI-8 (Serena fit) is principled — rather than expanding the open-question surface, the addition of GitNexus actually sharpens an existing open question by filling a slot that was previously implicitly contested. The retention of all 35 AC IDs without renumbering is the right call; in-place scope extension preserves traceability for downstream Plan and Test authoring.

The two new Use Cases (case 7 'GitNexus unavailable; documented fallback exercised'; case 8 reframing the 'eighth MCP six months later' narrative to cover the seven-server precedent) are well-placed and concretize the ADR-0018 fallback-visibility commitment in operator-facing terms.
